as the Dutch author Corrie Ten Boom used to say, ‘He puts up a sign 
saying “No fishing.”’1
Not only does he wipe the slate clean, but he also brings us into 
a relationship with God as sons and daughters. Not all men and 
women are children of God in this sense, although all of us were 
created by God. It is only to those who receive Jesus, to those who 
believe in his name, that he gives the ‘right to become children of 
God’ (John 1:12). Sonship in the New Testament (which is used in the 
generic sense to include sons and daughters) is not a natural status, 
but a spiritual one. We become sons and daughters of God not by 
being born, but by being born again by the Spirit.  
The book of Romans has been described as the Himalayas of the New 
Testament. If this is the case, then Chapter 8 is Mount Everest, and 
verses 14–17 could well be described as its peak.
